tasks.title: plugin-task-ui-2 — Typed SwiftUI-style builder SDK
tasks.description:
# Typed, SwiftUI-style builder SDK over `ViewNode`

An ergonomic authoring layer over the uniform node. Lives in **`heca-view`**, so a plugin can depend
on it — that crate has no dependencies but serde, which is the whole reason it exists.

## ⚠️ The original one-line description was written before the vocabulary was corrected

It said `Column::new().gap(8).child(...)`. **`Column` is not a kind any more.** F003/P017/T006
renamed `WidgetKind::Column` → `VStack` and `Row` → `HStack`, and gave **`Row`** to grid-ui's real
clickable, selectable widget. Builders must follow the corrected vocabulary or this SDK would
reintroduce exactly the confusion that rename removed.

## ✅ DECIDED BY THE USER 2026-07-27

**1. A type per widget kind.** One builder struct per `WidgetKind`, so a method exists only where
the widget really has that property — `Label::new("x").title("y")` is a **compile error**, not a
silently-ignored prop. The shared `Layout`/`Visual` properties come from **one trait implemented for
every builder**, written once, because after F003/P017/T007 those apply to every kind generically.
Rejected: a single generic `node(Kind)` builder — less code, but a nonsense method still compiles.

Target shape:

```rust
use heca_view::build::*;

let tree = VStack::new()
    .gap(8)
    .child(
        Panel::new().title("CONTAINERS").child(
            Row::new()
                .padding(6)
                .on_press(Intent::new("docker.select").arg("id", "web"))
                .child(Label::new("nginx"))
                .child(Badge::new("UP")),
        ),
    )
    .child(Separator::new())
    .child(Input::new().placeholder("filter…").name("q"))
    .into_node();
```

**2. Hand-written, with a drift guard — not generated.** A test in **`heca-view-realize`** (the one
crate depending on both `heca-view` and `heca-grid-ui`) walks `WidgetKind::ALL` against each widget's
`PROP_NAMES` and fails when a builder is missing a property the widget exposes. Fails **closed**, like
`heca-grid-ui/tests/prop_drift.rs`: a new property must reach the SDK unless someone names an
exception and says why. `heca-view` keeps zero dependencies — the guard lives above it.

---

# 📋 INVENTORY — taken 2026-07-27 from the compiler, not from reading. DO NOT RE-DERIVE.

**The guard needs no source parsing.** `PROP_NAMES` / `HOST_ONLY_BUILDERS` are **trait consts on
`SetProp`** (`heca-grid-ui/src/prop.rs:68`), so `<Row as SetProp>::PROP_NAMES` is readable from any
crate above `heca-grid-ui`. That is how this list was produced (a throwaway test in
`heca-view-realize/tests/`), and it is how the guard should read it — `prop_drift.rs` parses sources
only because it must catch builders that have *no* surface at all.

## The shared half — every field is settable by name through `merge_style_half`

**`Layout` (34):** align, align_self, direction, flex_grow, flex_shrink, gap, gap_spacing,
grid_cell, height, hidden, justify, justify_items, justify_self, margin, margin_bottom,
margin_left, margin_right, margin_top, max_height, max_width, min_height, min_width, pad_spacing_x,
pad_spacing_y, padding, padding_bottom, padding_left, padding_right, padding_top, padding_x,
padding_y, size, size_explicit, width

**`Visual` (6):** border, fill, font_scale, font_size, glow, radius

### Findings the Style trait has to deal with

- **`width`/`height`/`min_*`/`max_*` are `Length`**, whose wire form is: a **number** → px, the
  string **`"auto"`**, or a string like **`"50%"`** (`heca-grid-ui/src/style.rs:141` — custom
  Serialize/Deserialize). So the typed setters are `.width(240)`, `.width_pct(0.5)`,
  `.width_auto()`, and there is no need for a `Length` mirror in the model.
- **`border` and `glow` CANNOT be authored today.** They are structs (`Border{color,width}`,
  `Glow{color,radius,intensity}`) and **`PropValue` has no map/object variant** — only Bool, Int,
  Float, Text, Size, Variant, Align, Color, Glyph, List. So they are exceptions with a real reason,
  not an oversight. (`fill` and `radius` *are* proven authorable — tests at
  `heca-view-realize/src/lib.rs:1301` and `:1370`.) If they should become authorable, that is a
  `PropValue` change and its own task.
- **Do not expose:** `size_explicit` (set by the layout pass, not an author), `direction` (the kind
  already says it — `HStack` with `direction: column` is a contradiction), `grid_cell` (Grid
  placement is authored as `area`/`col`/`row` props read by the Grid arm), `pad_spacing_*` /
  `gap_spacing` (theme `Spacing` tokens, no model mirror — see the open question).

## The per-kind half — `PROP_NAMES` with real parameter types

| Widget | Properties (type) |
|---|---|
| Alert | variant(`AlertVariant`), body(String) |
| Badge | variant(`BadgeVariant`) |
| BadgeButton | variant(`BadgeVariant`) |
| Button | icon(`Glyph`), variant(`ButtonVariant`), font_size(f32), glow(bool), bordered(bool) |
| Checkbox | checked(bool), label(String), label_side(`LabelSide`) |
| Choice | selected(bool) |
| DockFrame | frameless(bool), expanded(bool), active(bool), nav_selected(bool) |
| Gauge | value(f32) |
| Icon | size(f32), color(`Color`), secondary_color(`Color`), glow(bool) |
| IconButton | cell(f32), tone(`Color`), glow(bool), active(bool) |
| Input | font_size(f32), value(String), placeholder(String) |
| Item | font_size(f32), active(bool), marker(`ActiveMarker`), muted(bool), leading_bordered(bool), trailing_bordered(bool) |
| ItemGroup | expanded(bool) |
| Label | align(`TextAlign`), color(`Color`), bold, italic, underline, strikethrough (bool), font_size(f32), font_scale(f32) |
| MarkerGroup | active(bool), nav_selected(bool) |
| Panel | title(String) |
| RailCell | cell_size(f32), active(bool) |
| Row | highlight(`Color`), attention_color(`Color`), active(bool), marker(`ActiveMarker`), nav_selected(bool) |
| ScrollRegion | axes(`ScrollAxes`) |
| Select | font_size(f32), selected(usize) |
| Separator | orientation(`Orientation`), length(f32) |
| Tabs | font_size(f32), selected(usize) |
| Tag | color(`Color`) |
| Toast | severity(`ToastSeverity`), icon(`Glyph`), body(String), dismissible(bool) |
| Toggle | on(bool) |

**`Card` and `StatusDot` do not implement `SetProp` at all** — no kind-specific properties; their
builders are the shared trait plus (for Card) children.

Kinds whose widget is on `prop_drift`'s `NO_SURFACE_REQUIRED` list also have none: VStack/HStack
(`Flex`), Surface, Grid, ScrollBar (host-only).

## Events, per kind — only the ones `realize` actually reads

- **press:** Row, Button, IconButton, BadgeButton, Item, RailCell, Choice
- **change:** Input, Toggle, Checkbox, Select, Tabs
- **toggle:** ItemGroup, DockFrame
- **action + dismiss:** Toast

A builder should expose only its own events, on the same principle as its properties. Note the
compiler cannot catch a wrong event *name* (it is a string in the model), so this mapping wants a
test: build through the SDK, realize, dispatch, assert the intent fires.

## Which kinds take children

VStack, HStack, Row, Grid, Card, Scroll, Panel, Surface, ItemGroup, DockFrame, MarkerGroup, Tabs,
Select (its options are `Choice` children), Choice, Button (its content is its children), Item
(slots). **Toast takes none** — asserted by an existing test. Leaves: Label, Badge, Tag, Icon,
Input, Toggle, Checkbox, StatusDot, Gauge, Separator, RailCell, Alert, ScrollBar.

# ❓ OPEN SUB-QUESTION — put to the user before writing the builders

**Six enum-valued properties have no mirror in `heca-view`:** `ActiveMarker` (Row, Item),
`ScrollAxes` (Scroll), `Orientation` (Separator), `LabelSide` (Checkbox), `ToastSeverity` (Toast),
`AlertVariant` (Alert) — plus `TextAlign` (Label) and `Glyph` (Button/Toast/Icon).

They travel as **their name in snake_case** (the model's own rule; `PropInput::Text(prop_enum_name(..))`).
So a typed builder either:

- **(a)** takes `&str` for these — no new model types, but `Separator::new().orientation("vertcal")`
  compiles and silently does nothing, which is the class of defect F003/P010/T006 spent a whole
  task removing from actions; or
- **(b)** adds mirror enums to `heca-view` alongside the existing `ViewVariant` / `ViewAlign` /
  `ViewSize` — genuinely typed, at the cost of ~6 small enums and a mapping each in `realize`
  (the mapping may already exist there: check, since props currently arrive as text).

**(b) looks right** and matches why `ViewVariant`/`ViewAlign`/`ViewSize` exist at all, but it widens
the task and the user has NOT been asked yet. Do not pick it alone.

tasks.title: Keyboard scrolling acts on whatever has focus — one branch, plus the four horizontal actions
tasks.description:
# Keyboard scrolling for any scroll area

# ✅ SHIPPED — the widget half (`096f06e`), unchanged by anything below

Eight `WidgetIntent` variants: `ScrollPageUp` / `ScrollPageDown` / `ScrollToTop` / `ScrollToBottom`
and the four horizontal ones. `ScrollRegion` acts on them:

- it owns the arithmetic — a page is 0.9 of its viewport, the edges clamp — because it is the only
  thing that knows its viewport and its content;
- it **declines** an axis it cannot scroll (axis off, or content fits), so a nested region or the host
  gets a turn; consuming would make the key silently do nothing;
- handled after the children, so the innermost scrollable region wins, as with the wheel;
- `keyboard_target(Signal<bool>)` gates which instance responds — per instance, position-agnostic,
  unset means yes. Bound to the mount's chrome focus by F003/P011/T020
  (`StateView::container_keyboard_target`).

**The logic lives in the widget, once.** Every `ScrollRegion` anywhere behaves identically with no
per-usage code. The host only ever says "one page down, this axis".

# ⚠️ THE ROUTE CHANGED — 2026-07-29, by the user. This supersedes the 2026-07-16/27 keys.

**Superseded:** vertical `prefix+Home/End/PageUp/PageDown`, horizontal `prefix+Shift+` the same four.
That shape existed because there was no other way to stop the keys reaching the terminal.

**Now:** *focus is the mode* (P085(F007) — "Components declare their actions; chrome focus is the
mode"). While a component holds chrome focus nothing is forwarded to a backend, so **plain
`PageUp` / `PageDown` / `Home` / `End` are free** and are the container's scroll keys; the existing
`Shift+` variants stay exactly as they are for the focused *pane*'s scrollback.

**And it is not a new action family.** The bindings already exist and are already global/direct:
`scroll_page_up = "Shift+PageUp"`, `scroll_page_down`, `scroll_to_top = "Shift+Home"`,
`scroll_to_bottom = "Shift+End"`, `scroll_line_up/down` (`keybindings.default.toml`), handled today
against the focused terminal viewport. So the app half is:

1. **One branch at the top of those existing handlers**: chrome focus set ⇒ dispatch the matching
   `Event::Widget(WidgetIntent::Scroll*)` into the chrome tree — the FocusScope (P085/T351) delivers it
   to the focused container and every other container is inert — else the terminal viewport path,
   unchanged. One binding, one meaning: *scroll whatever has focus*.
2. **The four horizontal actions** still need adding (`ScrollPageLeft/Right`, `ScrollToLeftEdge/RightEdge`
   — the widget intents exist, no `WmAction` does), through the full Adding-New-Actions checklist
   (AGENTS.md): variant → `action_from_name` → `action_priority` → `action_policy()` → handler →
   `build_registry` → `keybindings.default.toml` → `ActionRegistry::ALL` descriptor **with its `args`
   declaration** → `rpc.rs` → README. Reuse `ResizeAxis` (`heca/src/input.rs:40`) if an axis argument is
   preferred over four names — optional, defaulting to vertical, so a plain binding stays legal
   (a *required* argument would forbid a bare key, F003/P010/T006).
3. A **declined** intent stops at the chrome; it does **not** fall through to the pane. The
   innermost-wins rule is about nested *scroll areas*, and the pane is not an outer scroll area of the
   sidebar.

**This half is specified in P085(F007)/T352 step 5** (the routing task) — whichever is picked up first,
do not implement it twice. What remains uniquely here is the horizontal action family.

# Still ruled out (2026-07-28, checked in code — do not re-open)

Feeding these through the **widget keymap** (`build_widget_keymap`, `heca/src/app/registry.rs:202`,
the `[keys.widgets]` table). It is consulted at `heca/src/app/events.rs:156` inside a branch that
requires **a modal to be open**, so `[keys.widgets]` reaches focused widgets inside modals only.

# The 2026-07-17 blocker is discharged

"No chrome surface mounts a `ScrollRegion`" is false since 2026-07-26: containers nest their own
(`heca/src/providers/workspaces.rs`). `GridKey` still has no `PageUp`/`PageDown` — and does not need
it, because the intent is semantic. That is the point of not delivering a key.

# Acceptance

- With a container focused, plain `PageUp/PageDown/Home/End` scroll **it**; with a pane focused, the
  `Shift+` variants scroll the pane's scrollback, as today.
- Every other scroll area declines; nothing reaches the terminal while a container is focused.
- Horizontal scrolling reachable from RPC through the same actions, one code path.
- No second mechanism for the same job.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings.
- **USER verifies in the app**, with more than one scroll area on screen (P085(F007)/T359 seats the
  second one).

**USER DECISION (2026-07-25): unify BOTH chrome and placement.** I recommended leaving the Tooltip alone (a tooltip is not a panel; a `place_beside` authority would have exactly one caller — YAGNI) and flagged the risk. The user chose full unification. Their call; implemented in full rather than half-done.

WHAT WAS BUILT (uncommitted — pending the user's eyes on the GPU showcase):
1. **`place_beside(anchor, panel, viewport, gap, side) -> Rectangle`** in `heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/overlay.rs` — the THIRD placement authority, beside `place_anchored_on` (rect, leading-edge aligned, below↔above) and `place_at_point` (point, corner-offset, down-right↔up-left). `place_beside` is the rect + **centered cross-axis** + all-four-sides rule. They are three functions, not one with flags, because they differ in ALIGNMENT — documented as a table in the rustdoc and in docs/widgets.md.
2. **`BesideSide { Top | Bottom | Left | Right }`** — no `Auto` variant, deliberately: "beside" has no natural default direction the way a dropdown has "below". Private `opposite()` + `fits()` helpers on the enum.
3. **`TooltipSide` is now `pub type TooltipSide = BesideSide;`** — a true alias, not a second enum, so the two can never disagree about what `Top` means. All 5 external call sites (showcase ×3, heca/src/chrome/mod.rs, heca/src/providers/workspaces.rs, tests) compile unchanged.
4. **`Tooltip::fits` + the body of `bubble_rect` DELETED** (~40 lines) → `bubble_rect` is now a one-line delegation to `place_beside`.

Clamping the main axis would slide the bubble OVER the target it describes. When neither side fits, the preferred side is kept and the panel overflows. Locked by `beside_keeps_the_preferred_side_when_neither_fits`. (`place_anchored_on` DOES clamp its main axis — the two rules differ on purpose.)

Written as a "purity note" section in the rustdoc and as a ⚠️ callout in docs/widgets.md: draw-only, or don't use it.

═══ COMMITTED f2f65de (2026-07-24) — awaiting final user re-test ═══
`Overlay::panel_size(width, height)` + `Dialog::panel_size(..)`. Order-independent (stored on the Overlay and re-applied when `panel()`/`panel_boxed()` replaces the child), opt-in (unset = hug content). `Length::Pct` resolves against the VIEWPORT (the Overlay fills it); `Px` pins.

WHY THE TWO HALVES ARE ONE FEATURE: a ScrollRegion only scrolls when its parent BOUNDS it. An unsized panel grows with its content, so nothing overflows and no scrollbar appears.

═══ FOUR BUGS FOUND WHILE VERIFYING — all fixed in the WIDGETS, not pushed onto callers ═══
1. **ScrollRegion could not shrink below its content** ⇒ it overflowed its parent instead of scrolling (user: "content still overflow the modal, it should show scrollbars"). TWO causes, both in `Style`: (a) no `min_size` mapping at all, so taffy used its default `min: auto` = the item's CONTENT size; (b) a blanket `flex_shrink: 0.0` ("never let a flex container squish widgets"). FIX: `Style` gains `min_width`/`min_height`/`max_width`/`max_height` (Option<Length>) + `flex_shrink: Option<f32>` (None ⇒ 0.0, preserving the old rule); `ScrollRegion::new()` sets min 0 / shrink 1 ON ITSELF — being smaller than its content is what a viewport IS, not a caller setting.
2. **Panel could exceed the window** and get cut by the screen edge (user: "modal bigger than the main window"). FIX: `Overlay::apply_panel_size` now ALWAYS caps the panel at `Pct(1.0)` (unconditional, not only when panel_size is set), and the Overlay carries `padding = VIEWPORT_MARGIN (24.0)` so the cap resolves against an inset content box ⇒ a maxed panel keeps a margin instead of having its border/glow shaved (user: "should leave a little margin around").
3. **Wheel never reached a ScrollRegion inside a modal; thumb drag stuck to the cursor** (user: "Wheel not works. When click and drag mouse cannot be released anymore"). CAUSE: `Dialog::event` and `Overlay::event` only offered `Scroll` to `overlay_active` descendants (a ScrollRegion is NOT one) and neither routed `PointerReleased` AT ALL (it fell to the `_ => Handled::No` catch-all), so the grab never ended. FIX: both route Scroll to the panel first (then the modal swallow keeps the page behind still) and route PointerReleased to the panel.
4. **Rows cut on the left** (user-reported twice). CAUSE: ScrollRegion clipped to EXACTLY its bounds, but every bordered surface paints a rest-glow halo OUTSIDE its own bounds (T011) ⇒ a child flush against the edge had its halo scissored. FIX: widen the clip by GLOW_BLEED on an axis the region does NOT scroll — only the scrolling axis needs a tight cut. Plus default `padding_y` + row `gap` inside the region (user: "internal children should have more y margin around").

CALLER BURDEN REMOVED (user: "this should be internal calculation not something developers or agents should be setting on every modal"): `Dialog::body()`/`body_boxed()` call `fit_body()`, which fills the panel width and takes the leftover height — only when the caller left them at defaults. So the whole caller side is now:
    Dialog::new(t).panel_size(Px(560), Px(420)).body(ScrollRegion::new().child(..)).action(..)

MEASURED (probe, viewport 2000x1400, panel 560x420): panel = 560x420 exactly; ScrollRegion child = 524x300 (bounded, gets the leftover); action row inside the panel. Sizing/bounding verified numerically, not by eye.

tasks.title: SDF glyph/text glow renderer — Icon + RailCell rest glow
tasks.description:
Split out of T014 (2026-07-24). USER-REQUESTED follow-up to T011 (rest glow, 7ff3b59 + 319a349). RENDERER work.

THE GAP: T011 gave every bordered SURFACE a faint rest glow, but a GLYPH could not carry one — `TextCmd` had no glow field and glow lived only in the SDF rect renderer.

═══ TECHNIQUE — DECIDED BY USER 2026-07-25: (a) ADDITIVE HALO PASS ═══
Options presented were (a) additive halo pass, (b) true SDF text atlas, (c) offscreen bloom. User chose (a). Rejected for now: (b) is a multi-session change that puts the TERMINAL glyph path (the hottest in the app) at risk; (c) duplicates F004/P002/T001 "Implement offscreen bloom pipeline", which is a real but unstarted task — building it here would have been the wrong task id.

FACTS VERIFIED IN CODE BEFORE BUILDING (the task's 2026-07-17 line numbers were stale):
- Glyph atlas is R8Unorm COVERAGE with `PAD: u32 = 1` (atlas.rs:17) ⇒ a multi-tap blur READ in the fragment shader would bleed into neighbouring atlas entries. That is why the halo is offset COPIES, not a shader blur.
- Text pipeline uses `PREMULTIPLIED_ALPHA_BLENDING` (text.rs) and the fragment returned `(rgb*a, a)` ⇒ emitting `a == 0` with `rgb > 0` is exactly additive — the same trick grid.wgsl:146 uses for rect glow. This is what makes the halo read as light rather than as a grey smear.
- `Icon::paint` already stacked TWO glyph layers, so a halo layer is a third, not a new mechanism.

═══ BUILT 2026-07-25 — UNCOMMITTED, AWAITING GPU VERIFICATION ═══
ARCHITECTURE: the SCENE asks for a glow DECLARATIVELY (`TextCmd.glow: Option<Glow>`, mirroring `RectCmd.glow`); the RENDERER decides how to realize it. Swapping the multi-tap for a true SDF pass later changes no widget and no scene code.

heca-grid-ui:
- `scene.rs` — `TextCmd.glow: Option<Glow>`.
- `component.rs` — `PaintCx::icon_glowing(rect, glyph, color, size, glow)`; `icon()` delegates with `None`. Applies `scaled_glow` INTERNALLY, so the glyph halo goes through the ONE chokepoint (no second glow scale).
- `component.rs` — `PaintCx::with_content_glow(Option<Glow>, f)` + `content_glow()`. The halo counterpart of `with_content_color`, added for the same reason: a control holds children as `impl Component` and cannot style them, so it PUBLISHES and the glyph PULLS.
- `widgets/icon.rs` — `Icon::glow(bool)` (default false). Opt-in, NOT automatic: most icons sit inside an already-glowing control, so haloing all of them would double the light. Resolution order mirrors colour: own opt-in → inherited content glow → flat. Only the PRIMARY layer haloes (haloing the secondary wash too would double the light on every duotone glyph for a second set of taps). `HALO_RADIUS = 6.0` (tighter than a surface's — a glyph's strokes are thin, a wide halo reads as a smudge).
- `widgets/rail_cell.rs` — publishes `rest_glow(ICON_HALO_RADIUS)` for its subtree ONLY at rest (hover/active/disabled already have lit chrome). This is the "RailCell bare-icon rest glow" the task asked for, achieved without RailCell reaching into its child.

heca-renderer:
- `text.rs` — `TextGlow { color, radius, intensity }` + `TextGlow::is_visible()` (the SINGLE definition of "inert", used by both emission and cache hashing). `TextCommand.glow`; `queue_text_in_box` gained the parameter (its only caller is scene.rs). `queue_text` / `queue_text_in_line_box_with_style` pass None. `queue_terminal_run` hard-codes None with the reason in a comment.
- `text.rs` — `TextVertex.additive: f32` + `shader_location: 3` on BOTH pipelines. `EmitKey.glow_bits` (halo quads are baked into cached vertices, so a glow change must miss the cache).
- `text.rs` — emission rewritten: a `push_quad` closure (kills the 4x vertex duplication), `HALO_TAPS = 8` copies on a ring of `radius * HALO_OFFSET_FRAC (0.35)`, per-tap alpha = `color.a * intensity / HALO_TAPS` so the taps SUM BACK to the requested strength instead of blowing out 8x. Halo emitted BEFORE the sharp glyphs. **The ink bbox is grown by the ring reach** — otherwise damage/clip culling would scissor away the very light the halo adds outside the glyph box (the task's damage-model edge case).
- `text.wgsl` — `additive` through vertex→fragment; `out_a = a * (1.0 - additive)`.
- `scene.rs` — maps `TextCmd.glow` → `TextGlow`.

BUG FOUND BY MY OWN TEST: `glow_bits` hashed the raw colour even for an INERT glow (alpha 0 / radius 0), so two commands producing identical output (no halo) got different cache keys and would rebuild geometry every frame. Also the "is it visible" predicate was DUPLICATED between emission and hashing and could drift. Fixed by extracting `TextGlow::is_visible()` and filtering through it in both places.

**Completion summary:**
═══ CLOSED 2026-07-25 — delivered + user-verified ("now its fine") ═══

TECHNIQUE — the user first chose (a) an additive multi-tap halo. That was BUILT, then ABANDONED after visual verification, and replaced with a **blurred glyph in the atlas** (also user-approved). Recording why, so nobody rebuilds the discarded one:

**Why the ring of copies failed** (4 rounds of GPU verification): a ring is a DISCRETE shell, so the copies read as spokes and arcs, never as light. It also degraded as the radius grew — a fixed tap count spreads thinner, and at `glow_size = large` the copies became a countable lattice. Deriving the tap count from ring circumference fixed the lattice but not the shells. Two rings, 12–46 taps, four tuning constants — still structurally wrong. **Do not reintroduce it.**

═══ WHAT SHIPPED ═══
`Atlas::glyph_blurred(.., sigma)` rasterizes the glyph's coverage mask, pads by 3σ, blurs (three box passes ≈ Gaussian), **renormalizes the peak back to full coverage**, and stores it as its own atlas entry keyed by `(glyph, sigma bucket)`. Emission draws ONE quad per glyph sampling it.
- 24–92 quads/glyph → **1**. Continuous falloff by construction. σ scales with `glow_size` for free.
- `Atlas::clear()` drops the blurred cache too (its UVs would otherwise dangle).
- `PlacedGlyph` carries its `CacheKey` — the layout is cached independently of any glow, so the blurred variant can only be resolved at emission.

heca-grid-ui: `TextCmd.glow` (declarative, mirroring `RectCmd.glow` — the renderer decides how to realize it); `PaintCx::icon_glowing` (applies `scaled_glow` internally = the ONE chokepoint); `PaintCx::with_content_glow`/`content_glow` (halo counterpart of `with_content_color`: a control holds children as `impl Component` and cannot style them, so it publishes and the glyph pulls); `Icon::glow(bool)` opt-in; `RailCell` publishes at rest only.
heca-renderer: `TextGlow` + `is_visible()`; `TextVertex.additive` + `shader_location: 3` on both pipelines; `EmitKey.glow_bits` + `glow_mode_bits`; `text.wgsl` `out_a = a * (1.0 - additive)`; `TextRenderer::set_glow_alpha_scale` wired from `enqueue_scene`.

═══ THREE BUGS FOUND DURING VERIFICATION ═══
1. **Halo invisible at first (ring era).** Per-tap alpha was `intensity / HALO_TAPS` on the theory that taps "sum back". They sit on a ring and barely overlap, so each contributed 1.5% alpha. Wrong reasoning, not a typo.
2. **Halo vanished entirely on switching to the blur.** Blurring conserves energy, NOT peak: spreading a thin stroke over σ≈4px drops its peak to ~¼, so the halo came out at ~0.03 alpha. FIX: renormalize the blurred mask to full peak — which also makes `intensity` mean *peak alpha*, the same quantity a rect's glow peaks at, so the two are comparable instead of eyeballed. Locked by `a_blurred_mask_is_renormalized_back_to_full_peak`.
3. **Light theme absent.** `grid.wgsl` switches rect glow to a translucent tinted halo on light backgrounds (`glow_alpha_scale`) because ADDING light to a near-white surface does nothing. `enqueue_scene` already computed it; the text path ignored it. The glyph path now mirrors the rect's own curve (`sqrt(base) * glow_alpha_scale`) rather than a linear scale.
Plus a doc bug: `with_content_glow` claimed the published glow was pre-scaled. It is not — `rest_glow()` returns unscaled and the chokepoint scales once; the doc would have led to double-scaling.

═══ CALIBRATION — the load-bearing insight ═══
Matching a lit surface means matching **emitted light**, not peak alpha. Perceived glow scales with the emitting PERIMETER: a glyph's is ~¼ of a button's, so identical peak + identical radius still looks dimmer and tighter (user: "do you see the icon button glow the same as the Top/Bottom/Left/Right buttons?" — no). Final values sit deliberately ABOVE parity, and each constant's rustdoc says so, so they are not "corrected" back later:
- `HALO_RADIUS_FRAC = 0.55` of glyph size (34px glyph → 18.7px reach; Button's rest glow is 12.0). Derived from glyph size, not fixed — a 20px toolbar icon must not get the same absolute halo as a 34px one.
- `HALO_DARK_GAIN = 1.6` (peak 0.189), `HALO_LIGHT_GAIN = 1.6` (peak 0.341). Moved together so the themes cannot drift.

tasks.title: A property value can hold an object, so appearance is really authorable
tasks.description:
# The hole

`Visual` has six fields: `fill`, `border`, `glow`, `radius`, `font_size`, `font_scale`
(`heca-grid-ui/src/style.rs:276`). **Two of them cannot be set from a description, and never could.**

`border` is `Border { color, width }` and `glow` is `Glow { color, radius, intensity }`
(`heca-grid-ui/src/scene.rs:271` and `:280`). A property value is a **closed list of scalars** —
`Bool, Int, Float, Text, Size, Variant, Align, Color, Glyph, List`
(`heca-view/src/lib.rs:218`). There is no object, so there is no way to write `{color, width}`.

**F003/P017/T007 claimed otherwise.** Its commit `eb9e021` says "the whole of `Visual` — fill,
border, glow, radius, font size, font scale". It gave `Border` and `Glow` serde derives, which made
them look reachable. Serde on the type is not the same as a property value that can carry it.
Four fields work; the commit says six. Nothing tested the two, so nothing failed.

This is the exact defect class F003/P017 existed to close, and it survived the phase.

# Why this blocks F003/P011/T006

The typed builder SDK is meant to make a wrong property a compile error. Built on today's
`PropValue` it would instead ship an exceptions list saying "border and glow cannot be authored" —
freezing the hole into a compile-checked API, which is precisely why T006 was split out of this
phase in the first place (see its status log, 2026-07-25).

# What to build

**`PropValue::Map(PropMap)`** in `heca-view/src/lib.rs`. `PropMap` is already
`BTreeMap<String, PropValue>` (`heca-view/src/lib.rs:260`), so the variant is recursive for free and
**no future struct-valued field needs another variant** — that is the point. Serde is externally
tagged with `rename_all = "snake_case"`, so it travels as `{"map": {...}}`.

**`prop_to_json` must recurse** (`heca-view-realize/src/lib.rs:208`). It already recurses for
`List` at `:226`. A `Map` becomes a JSON object, and — this is the part to get right — **a colour
token nested inside it must still resolve**: `border = {color: "accent", width: 2}` has to go
through `resolve_color` (`:221`, `:233`) at any depth, not just at the top level. Without that, a
nested colour silently becomes the literal string "accent" and the field fails to deserialize.

**Totality still holds.** `merge_style_half` (`heca-view-realize/src/lib.rs`) drops a value that
does not fit its field *individually* — one bad property never discards the good ones and never
panics. A malformed nested object must behave the same way; there is an existing test for the flat
case (`a_bad_colour_does_not_discard_its_neighbours`, `:1449`).

**Not in scope:** `PropInput` (`heca-grid-ui/src/prop.rs:27`) stays `Bool | Number | Text`.
That is the *widget-property* channel, and no widget builder takes a struct today. `border`/`glow`
are `Visual` fields, which reach the widget through `merge_style_half` and serde, not through
`PropInput`. If a widget ever needs a struct property, that is a separate change — record it, do not
pre-build it.

# Steps

1. Add the variant + doc it as the extension point for any struct-shaped field.
2. Recurse in `prop_to_json`, resolving colours at any depth.
3. Tests in `heca-view-realize`: a described `border` reaches the widget; a described `glow` does;
   a **token name** nested inside one resolves against the theme; a malformed nested object drops
   only itself.
4. **Fix the record.** T007's claim is repeated wherever appearance is documented — check
   `docs/chrome-and-ui.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the `Visual` doc comments, and correct anything that
   says all of `Visual` was reachable before this task.
5. Then unblock F003/P011/T006 and let the SDK expose `border`/`glow` like any other property.

# Acceptance

- A `ViewNode` can set `border` and `glow`, proven by a test that asserts the value on the realized
  widget, not merely that it parses.
- A theme token nested inside an object resolves.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings.

---
**Completion summary:**
# ✅ DONE 2026-07-27 — commit `f2deecd`

`PropValue::Map(PropMap)` in `heca-view/src/lib.rs`. Recursive, so **no future struct-shaped
property needs another variant** — that was the point, not `border`/`glow` specifically.

- `prop_to_json` (`heca-view-realize/src/lib.rs:208`) recurses, resolving a colour token **at any
  depth**. Without that a nested `"accent"` reaches serde as the literal word and the whole field is
  dropped, silently.
- `prop_to_input` rejects `Map` alongside `List`, with the reason on the arm: `PropInput` is the
  scalar channel for *widget* builders and no `#[prop]` builder takes a struct. `Visual` fields
  reach the widget through `merge_style_half` and serde instead. If a widget builder ever takes one,
  `PropInput` grows a variant then — deliberately, not pre-built.
- Totality holds at depth: a member that does not convert costs only itself.

**Three tests, asserting the value on the realized widget rather than that it parses**, and they
interlock: `a_bad_member_of_an_object_does_not_discard_the_rest` proves an unusable colour drops the
border; `a_token_nested_in_an_object_resolves_against_the_theme` proves `"accent"` yields the
theme's accent and follows a theme change. If resolution did not recurse, the second would take the
first's path and fail. Plus
`a_struct_shaped_appearance_property_reaches_the_widget` for border and glow together.

**The record was corrected**, which was half the point of the task: `AGENTS.md:753` and
`docs/chrome-and-ui.md` §R2 both repeated T7's "the whole of `Visual`". Both now state what was true
then, what is true now, and the lesson — **adding serde to a type is not the same as being able to
author it; check the value channel.**

964 tests, 0 failures, clippy 0 warnings. Nothing visual changed, so there was nothing for the user
to look at; the proof is the tests.

## Follow-up this exposed (not done here)

`PropValue` carries three hardcoded enum mirrors — `Size`, `Variant`, `Align` — which is the same
closed shape `Map` was added to escape: every new enum would want its own variant. It does not need
one. Fixed value sets travel as their **name**, so a `Text` carries any of them and the *type* lives
in the authoring layer. New mirrors added from here on must NOT get a `PropValue` variant. Collapsing
the existing three is a wire-format change and wants its own task.

tasks.title: Fixed value sets become types, so a misspelt one cannot compile
tasks.description:
# The hole

Several properties accept only a fixed set of words. In a description they are written as free text:

```rust
.prop("orientation", PropValue::Text("vertcal".into()))   // typo — compiles, silently ignored
```

The separator stays horizontal and nothing reports anything. This is the same silent failure
F003/P010/T006 spent a whole task removing from **actions** (a misspelt argument name did nothing
forever, one stderr line in debug and none in release). It is still live in the **UI vocabulary**.

Three value sets already have types in `heca-view` for exactly this reason — `ViewSize`,
`ViewVariant`, `ViewAlign`. The rest never got them.

# ✅ DECIDED BY THE USER 2026-07-27

**Give the small sets real types, and generate the glyph list.** Two separate answers because the
glyph set is not like the others.

## The small sets — measured, `heca-grid-ui`

| grid-ui type | Values | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `Orientation` (`widgets/separator.rs`) | Horizontal, Vertical | Separator.orientation |
| `ScrollAxes` (`widgets/scroll_region.rs`) | Vertical, Horizontal, Both | Scroll.axes |
| `ToastSeverity` (`widgets/toast.rs`) | Info, Success, Warning, Danger | Toast.severity |
| `AlertVariant` (`widgets/alert.rs`) | Info, Success, Warning, Danger | Alert.variant |
| `LabelSide` (`widgets/checkbox.rs`) | Right, Left | Checkbox.label_side |
| `ActiveMarker` (`widgets/item.rs`) | None, Bar, Check | Row.marker, Item.marker |
| `TextAlign` (`scene.rs`) | Start, Center, End | Label.align |

**`AlertVariant` and `ToastSeverity` have identical values** — one mirror (`ViewSeverity`) serves
both. So **six** new types, 21 values in total.

## ⚠️ They must NOT get `PropValue` variants

This is the lesson from F003/P011/T018, and it is the whole reason this task is small.

`PropValue` already carries three hardcoded mirrors (`Size`, `Variant`, `Align`) — the closed shape
`Map` was added to escape. **A fixed value set travels as its name**, so `PropValue::Text` carries
any of them and the *type* lives in the authoring layer. Give each mirror
`impl From<ViewOrientation> for PropValue` producing `Text(name)`, so `.prop("orientation",
ViewOrientation::Vertical)` reads well without `PropValue` learning anything.

Verified this works end to end: `prop_to_json` turns `Text` into a JSON string and the widget's own
enum deserializes from its snake_case name (`heca-view-realize/src/lib.rs:222`); `prop_to_input`
turns it into `PropInput::Text` and the generated `set_prop` parses the name
(`:299`). No realize change should be needed — confirm rather than assume.

Collapsing the existing three into this scheme is a wire-format change and wants its own task.

## Glyphs — generated, not copied

`Glyph` (`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/icon.rs:33`) has **52 variants and grows**. A hand-written mirror
is the "list nobody is forced to update" that this codebase keeps being bitten by.

Plan:
1. `Glyph::ALL` + a `name()` in `heca-grid-ui`, mirroring the `WidgetKind::ALL` pattern the model
   already uses. Useful on its own.
2. A **checked-in generated** `ViewGlyph` in `heca-view` — `heca-view` cannot depend on
   `heca-grid-ui` and must not start.
3. A drift test in **`heca-view-realize`** (the one crate that sees both) comparing `ViewGlyph`'s
   list against `Glyph::ALL` and failing when they diverge, naming what is missing. Same
   fails-closed shape as `prop_drift.rs`.

# Steps

1. Six mirrors in `heca-view`, serde `rename_all = "snake_case"`, each with `name()` and
   `From<_> for PropValue` → `Text`.
2. Confirm a realized widget actually receives each one (a test per mirror, asserting on the widget,
   not on the parse).
3. `Glyph::ALL` + `name()` in `heca-grid-ui`; generated `ViewGlyph` in `heca-view`; drift test in
   `heca-view-realize`.
4. Point the existing docs at the types where they currently show text values.

# Acceptance

- A misspelt value in any of the seven sets **does not compile** when written through a mirror.
- `heca-view` still depends on nothing but serde.
- The glyph list cannot silently disagree with `heca-grid-ui`'s.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings.
- Unblocks F003/P011/T006, whose builders can then be honestly typed.

---
**Completion summary:**
# ✅ DONE 2026-07-27 — commit `1653169`

Six mirrors in `heca-view`: `ViewOrientation`, `ViewScrollAxes`, `ViewSeverity`, `ViewLabelSide`,
`ViewMarker`, `ViewTextAlign`. Six not seven because `ToastSeverity` and `AlertVariant` carry the
same four values, and two copies of one list is how this codebase gets into trouble. A seventh,
**`ViewJustify`**, was added later in `7183250` — T019's inventory came from the widgets' own
properties and `justify` is a `Layout` field, so it never appeared.

**None of them has a `PropValue` variant, and the comment there says the next one must not either.**
A fixed set travels as its name, so `Text` carries every one of them and the type belongs in the
authoring layer. `Size`/`Variant`/`Align` predate that rule and are the closed shape `PropValue::Map`
was added to escape.

**Glyphs are generated, then held to account.** 52 names and growing, so `ViewGlyph` is generated and
`every_glyph_name_has_a_mirror` (`heca-view-realize`) compares it against the library's own list both
ways, naming what is missing. Verified by deleting a glyph and reading the failure:
`these glyphs exist in heca-grid-ui but not in ViewGlyph … ["backspace"]`. Nothing was needed in
`heca-grid-ui` — `Glyph::ALL` and the `PropName` derive already existed.

**Two guards on the names**, because agreement across two crates and a serde attribute is not
something to assume: `name()` and the serde spelling must match (checked over a list generated from
the same variants, so it cannot miss one), and every mirror is taken through `PropValue` into a
realized widget and asserted to change it — matching names is not the same as the name being
understood.

Docs: `docs/widgets.md` examples now use the types; `docs/chrome-and-ui.md` §R2 records the rule.

Nothing visual changed, so there was nothing for the user to look at; the proof is the tests.

tasks.title: Focus a dock by picking it: FocusDock through ActionRegistry + KeyHint
tasks.description:
# The bug this replaces

A sidebar is a **container** and left/right is a position. `handle_sidebar_focus`
(`heca/src/handlers.rs:1532`) reads `left_visible()` and calls `set_left_mode(Expanded)` — it names a
side. The workspaces dock declares `RegionSet::sidebars()`, so it may be seated on the right
(`heca/src/providers/workspaces.rs:66`), and then the focus key **expands the empty left container
and navigates a tree drawn on the right**. `state.sidebar_tree` carries no region either.

There is also no notion of chrome keyboard focus at all, and `Provider` has no focus concept
(`heca/src/providers/mod.rs`: id, supported_regions, default_region, default_order, title, movable,
collapsible, grow, build_contribution, context_menus, on_activate).

# ✅ DECIDED BY THE USER 2026-07-28 — pick a dock, through the existing machinery

**`FocusDock`: an action that hints every dock and focuses the one picked.** Built out of what is
already there, not a new subsystem:

- **`ActionRegistry`** owns the action, with its descriptor and its declared args (F003/P010/T006).
- **`KeymapRegistry`** binds it, so the key is configurable and never hardcoded — and because it is
  an action, **RPC can call it** like any other.
- **`KeyHint`** draws the letters. The workspaces dock already wraps each workspace in one
  (`KeyHint::new(dock).hint(..).placement(TopRight)`, `providers/workspaces.rs`), so a dock pick is
  the same idiom one level up.

## The shape

1. **`WmAction::FocusDock { dock: Option<ContainerId> }`** — one action, two ways in:
   - **bare** (`focus_dock`) → enters the pick: every mounted container lights a letter, press one
     and it takes focus. This is the keybinding case.
   - **with an id** (`focus_dock(dock="workspaces")`) → focuses it directly, no pick. This is the RPC
     and scripting case, and it falls out of the optional-argument machinery for free.
   Declared as `ArgDescriptor::optional_*`, so the bare binding stays legal (an action that *requires*
   an argument cannot carry one).
2. **Candidates come from the host**, not from a side: `ChromeHost::contributions(region)` over the
   regions, in the order the host maintains. Letters assigned as the other picks do
   (`pick_candidates` / `PendingPick`, `heca/src/chrome/state.rs`).
3. **Focus is state: a container id.** Not a side, not a dock's name written in code. Sticky, as
   focus is.
4. **Focus must be visible.** A focused container needs a ring or marker, or nothing tells the user
   where the keyboard is. This is a visual decision → the user judges it in the app.
5. **`Provider::keyboard_navigable()`** (default `false`) says whether a dock does anything with
   focus beyond scrolling. `WorkspacesContainerProvider` returns `true`. Knowledge of what can be
   navigated belongs to the provider.
6. **The old action stops naming a side.** `sidebar_focus` becomes focus-a-dock: with one navigable
   dock mounted it behaves as today; with none it is a no-op instead of expanding an empty container.

## What it unblocks

- **F003/P011/T012** app half: the scroll actions target the focused container. Its widget half is
  shipped (`096f06e`) — every `ScrollRegion` already acts on the intents and
  `ScrollRegion::keyboard_target(signal)` gates which one, per instance and position-agnostic. So the
  host sends one intent and the focused container's area takes it; every other declines.
- The dock's own navigation (the workspaces j/k cursor) follows the focused dock rather than a side.

# Steps

1. `Provider::keyboard_navigable()`; workspaces returns true.
2. Chrome keyboard focus state: `Option<ContainerId>`.
3. `WmAction::FocusDock { dock: Option<..> }` through the full Adding-New-Actions checklist
   (AGENTS.md): variant → `action_from_name` → `action_priority` → `action_policy()` → handler →
   `build_registry` → `keybindings.default.toml` → `ActionRegistry::ALL` descriptor **with its args
   declaration** → `rpc.rs` → README.
4. The pick: candidates from `ChromeHost`, letters via `KeyHint`, resolve → focus.
5. Bind each container's `ScrollRegion::keyboard_target` to `focus == my id`.
6. `sidebar_focus` stops naming a side.
7. Tests: focus survives the dock being moved between regions; no navigable dock → no-op; exactly one
   container is the keyboard target at a time; `focus_dock(dock="…")` needs no pick.
8. **USER verifies**: the letters appear over the docks, the picked one shows it has focus, and the
   scroll keys then act on it.

# Acceptance

- No side literal in the focus path.
- A container's wiring names no dock.
- `focus_dock` reachable from a keybinding **and** from RPC, the same action either way.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings.

---
**Completion summary:**
# ✅ DONE 2026-07-30 — verified in the app by the user

**Closed on what it set out to do: a dock can be picked by letter and takes focus, visibly.** The user
drove it and confirmed: *"FUC7F works... it brings us the hint to focus a container and it works."*
What is deliberately **not** here — being able to *do* anything with the focused container without
falling back to `prefix+e` — is the whole of **P085(F007) "Components declare their actions; chrome
focus is the mode"**, opened for exactly that reason. This task is not a partial delivery of that; it
is the state that phase builds on.

## What landed

- **Focus is a container id, not a side.** `SharedChromeState.focused_container` +
  `set_focused_container` (`heca/src/chrome/state.rs`), emitting `chrome.container.focus.changed`.
  Per-**mount** `keyboard_target` signals derived from it, so exactly one placement is the keyboard
  target by construction, and a signal asked for after focus moved is created already knowing.
- **`heca/src/chrome/focus.rs`** (new) — the two decisions as pure functions over `ChromeHost`:
  `dock_candidates(host, on_screen)` (letters, host order, on-screen regions only — a letter over a
  body nobody can see is a key that does nothing) and `navigable_dock(host, focused)` (which dock
  `sidebar_focus` acts on **and the region it sits in**).
- **The live bug is fixed.** `handle_sidebar_focus` no longer reads `left_visible()`; it asks the host
  for the navigable dock, reveals *that dock's* region (`reveal_region`), focuses it, then enters nav
  mode. With no navigable dock mounted it is a **no-op** instead of expanding an empty container.
- **`WmAction::FocusDock { dock: Option<ContainerId> }`** through the full Adding-New-Actions
  checklist: variant → `action_from_name` (bare ⇒ pick) → `build_action` (optional `dock` ⇒ direct) →
  `action_priority` → `handle_focus_dock` → `build_registry` → `keybindings.default.toml`
  (`prefix+Shift+e`) → descriptor with declared `args` → `rpc.rs` (`focus-dock [id]`) →
  `action_policy` = `Global` (chrome state, no layout impact; `SidebarFocus` stays `TiledOnly`) →
  README. An unknown id logs instead of vanishing.
- **The pick**: `InputMode::DockPick` (letter → container id), resolved in `app/input.rs` back out
  through the *same* `focus_dock` action carrying the id — the letter is only how a keyboard supplies
  an argument it cannot type. Status bar reads `FOCUS DOCK` with the action's own prompt.
- **`Provider::keyboard_navigable()`** (default `false`); `WorkspacesContainerProvider` returns `true`.
- **Library**: `FocusRing` — a generic transparent wrapper drawing the theme's focus outline from a
  host signal (a control owns its focus and rings itself; an *area* the keyboard is aimed at has no
  owner in the tree). Same `PaintCx::focus_ring`, same tokens, respects `show_focus_border`. Plus
  `KeyHint::new_boxed` so a dynamically built subtree can be wrapped. Both documented (rustdoc +
  `docs/widgets.md`), showcase demo, prop-drift guard satisfied.
- **Wiring**: `build_region_content` wraps every container in `FocusRing(KeyHint(body))`; the ring
  binds the **same signal** the container's `ScrollRegion` takes as its `keyboard_target`, so the ring
  and the keys cannot disagree.

## The trap it hit, for the next reader

The wrappers reintroduced F003/P011/T021's failure one level down: a hugging wrapper measures its
child's *content* and a flex item's automatic minimum stops it shrinking back, so the dock measured
**1214px inside its 296px slot**. `pass_box_down` passes the box through each wrapper level, and only
when there **is** a share (`grow = 0.0` means "size me to my content" and a zero base size inside a
content-sized parent collapses it to nothing). Same `flex: 1 1 0` debt as `with_share`, documented as
such — **F004/P006/T010 still replaces both with one `share(n)` setter.**

Tests measure pixels, not flags (the T021 lesson): shares still divide 296/296 through the wrappers; a
content-sized container keeps its 120px; the focus ring is found in the painted scene and disappears
when focus moves elsewhere (same tree, one signal); the dock letter is stamped over the dock; focus
survives a `move_container`; no navigable dock ⇒ nothing to focus.

## Left open, on purpose

- **Interaction** — the whole of P085(F007).
- A click that focuses an *arbitrary* dock: the mouse layer is still region-named
  (`MouseLeftSidebar` / `mouse/surface_left.rs`), so only the sidebar-nav click path focuses (via
  `SidebarFocus`). P085(F007)/T354 removes that naming.
- Only one container was on screen, so "a letter per dock" and "focus moving between docks" were not
  demonstrable. P085(F007)/T359 seats the second one.

Workspace green (1009 tests, was 985), clippy 0 warnings.

tasks.title: Containers scroll by nesting their own scroll area; fractional heights
tasks.description:
# The model (from the user, 2026-07-27)

A **scroll area is a container**. It can be nested anywhere — including inside another container, for
whatever widgets that one holds. So scrolling is **composed**, not a property some layer owns:

```
┌─ sidebar (a shell) ─┐
│ ┌─────────────────┐ │
│ │ container 1     │ │  ½ height, nests its own scroll area
│ └─────────────────┘ │
│ ┌─────────────────┐ │
│ │ container 2     │ │  ½ height, nests its own scroll area
│ └─────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────┘
```

**My earlier framing of this task was wrong** and is corrected here: it said the shell must stop
scrolling and its scroll area must be *moved* into the container. Nothing is misplaced. A shell may
have one, a container inside it may have its own, and nesting already decides which acts — the
innermost that *can* scroll the axis wins, the outer gets it only when the inner declines. The wheel
works that way today and the keyboard intents shipped in `096f06e` follow the same order.

# What is actually missing

**No container nests a scroll area, so they all share the shell's.** `build_region_content`
(`heca/src/chrome/mod.rs:1464`) stacks every contribution into one `Flex::column().gap(8.0)`
(`:1481-1489`) and `build_sidebar_shell` wraps the stack in the shell's single `ScrollRegion`
(`:1541`) — the only one in the app crate. Two docks in a sidebar therefore scroll as one column:
scrolling the first slides the second off the bottom. That is a gap in composition, not a
misplacement.

# ✅ DECIDED BY THE USER 2026-07-27

- **Heights are fractional, never fixed.** A container in a shell takes a percentage / fraction of
  the available height (`½` and `½` for two), so it has bounds to scroll *within* and the split
  survives any window size. No px heights.
- **The offset's name must be generic.** `SharedChromeState.workspaces.scroll`
  (`heca/src/chrome/state.rs:168`) is wrong twice over: it is a **region-level** field named after a
  **single dock**, for a scroll area that belongs to the shell. Whatever nests a scroll area owns its
  own offset — key it by the container (or region) generically, never by a dock's name.
- **The right sidebar is the test bed, and it is temporary.** Put **two containers in the right
  sidebar, ½ / ½ height, each with its own scroll area, each holding the same workspaces dock content
  as the left** — real content that overflows, so independent scrolling can actually be seen. Once it
  is verified working, **the right sidebar goes back to empty**; its real features come later. Do not
  leave the test bed shipped.

# Detail to settle while building

The test bed wants the workspaces content **twice**. A provider is registered once and seated once,
and ids are unique, so decide how: two mounted instances with distinct ids, or the same container body
built twice for the test. Prefer whichever does not require special-casing the host — and if it does
require it, say so rather than bending the host for a temporary test bed.

# Steps

1. A container's body can nest its own scroll area, with its own offset, keyed generically.
2. Rename/rehome the shell's offset off `workspaces.scroll` to something generic.
3. Fractional height distribution for containers sharing a shell.
4. The right-sidebar test bed: two containers, ½ / ½, both scrolling, both holding the workspaces
   content.
5. **USER looks at it** — two scroll areas moving independently, and the split holding at different
   window sizes. This is layout; tests are not verification.
6. Strip the test bed once verified, leaving the right sidebar empty.

# Then

- **F003/P011/T020** (chrome keyboard focus) targets a **container**, not a side and not a region.
- **F003/P011/T012**'s app half routes scroll intents to the focused container. Its widget half needs
  no change: `ScrollRegion::keyboard_target` is per instance, so it fits a nested area as readily as a
  shell's.

# Acceptance

- Two containers in one sidebar scroll independently, with fractional heights.
- No scroll offset named after a dock.
- The right sidebar ends up empty again.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings.

---
**Completion summary:**
# ✅ DONE 2026-07-28 — verified in the app by the user

Scrolling is **composed**: a scroll area is a container, nested where scrolling belongs. Commits
`1f4b92d` `7b3a624` `fd403dd` `1d75cb3` `3084714` `8c65a54` `fcbba56` `95a894d`.

- **Every scroll area owns its offset, per placement.** Three were tangled into one field: the left
  shell used the workspaces *container's* offset, the right shell had none and forgot its position on
  every rebuild, and the container's own was keyed by container *kind* — so two placements would have
  scrolled together, invisible until there were two. Offsets are now keyed by **mount id** on the shared
  store, created on first ask so they outlive the retained tree. `WorkspacesScrollChanged` became
  `ContainerScrollChanged`, carrying which container moved.
- **The shell does not scroll.** A viewport measures content at natural height, so wrapping the stack
  left the containers content-sized (a share had nothing to divide) and took the wheel for the sidebar
  instead of the container under the cursor. `RegionState.scroll` and the shell's `scroll` parameter
  were added and then deleted in the same session — the real answer was that the shell should not
  scroll, not that it needed an offset of its own.
- **A container declares its share** as `grow` on the contribution, default `1.0`. Named `grow`, not
  `height_grow`, because `flex_grow` is main-axis relative — one number is height in a sidebar and
  width in a bar. The region applies it, since a share only means something relative to siblings a
  container cannot see.
- **A share had to divide the region, not the leftovers.** `flex_grow` distributes only positive free
  space, so two containers measured **1214px each inside a 600px body**. With a zero base size and
  permission to shrink (CSS `flex: 1 1 0`): **296px each**. Debt recorded — expressing a proportion by
  writing a fixed measure is wrong, and `Layout` has no `flex_basis` (**F004/P006/T010**).
- **Placing a container twice is two calls.** `WorkspacesContainerProvider::placed(id, region)`
  replaced a hardcoded id and default region; `BuildCx` carries the mount id, built per container
  rather than per region, so one plain `fn` still serves every placement and per-placement state has
  somewhere to live.
- **A rule between containers**, taking no share of the height (292 / 1 / 291 measured).
- **`margin_x` / `margin_y`** added for parity with padding, so a described tree can set a margin by
  axis instead of naming both sides.

**Verified by the user**: two containers half and half, scrolling independently, each its own
scrollbar. It took three attempts, and the test that passed in between asserted a `grow` *flag* while
the layout was visibly broken — the replacement measures pixels.

**Docs (requested explicitly):** `docs/widgets.md` gained container shares, scrolling-by-nesting and
`ScrollRegion`'s keyboard intents; the README states the model — widget / container / shell, left and
right being only position.

**The test bed is gone and stays gone** (`95a894d`, user decision 2026-07-28). The right sidebar is
empty until it has real features. Consequence for T012/T020: only one container is on screen, so a
single container is all that can be demonstrated — say so plainly rather than implying more.
